title: Incremental inference handshake & SDK playbook (PRD sketch)
body:
Context
This is a working PRD sketch to capture a session-first approach for incremental/streaming inference, lightweight client prefetch hints, and a deterministic tool-call handshake that balances low-latency partial results with structured output guarantees. Focus is hosted API + SDK ergonomics (JS/TypeScript primary), but surface design should be portable to other SDKs.

Problem statement
- Customers building interactive features struggle to: (a) receive usable partial output early, (b) reliably trigger and reconcile tool calls inside partially-emitted streams, and (c) get structured chunks (e.g., JSON or typed records) without brittle client-side parsing.
- Current SDK patterns either expose raw chunks (hard to reason about) or hide streaming semantics (losing latency wins).

Goals
- Design an incremental frame protocol that is: typed, idempotent for retries, and suitable for streaming transports (SSE/WebSocket).
- Offer SDK primitives that make tool calls and structured outputs first-class (session object, typed frames, checkpointing).
- Define client hints for safe prefetch and batching decisions so server can optimize kernels and routing.

Non-goals
- This doc does not define private deployment entitlements or SLA tiers. Not addressing offline-first clients in depth.

Proposal summary
1) Frame model (atomic unit in stream)
   - frame_type: one of [partial_text, structured_chunk, tool_handshake, tool_result, checkpoint, error]
   - session_id: opaque session UUID under which frames are scoped
   - seq: monotonically increasing int (per session) used for idempotency and resume
   - payload: string (for text) or JSON-stringified structured content for structured_chunk/tool frames

   Example frames (JSON over SSE line)
   {"frame_type":"partial_text","session_id":"s:123","seq":4,"payload":"...draft sentence..."}
   {"frame_type":"tool_handshake","session_id":"s:123","seq":7,"payload":"{\\\"tool\\\":\\\"search\\\",\\\"args\\\":{\\\"q\\\":\\\"best widget\\\"}}"}

2) Tool handshake protocol (deterministic routing and retry semantics)
   - Client initiates by sending 'tool_call_intent' in request metadata or a synchronous preflight.
   - Server emits tool_handshake frame with call_id + required auth/hints (e.g., plugin url, input schema).
   - Client/SDK may perform local validation and either accept or reject the handshake using an ack frame.
   - If accepted, server pauses text emission and emits tool_result frames when results arrive; tool_result frames contain call_id and a result_sequence inside payload.
   - All tool frames are idempotent by (session_id, call_id, seq). Retries from client should include last seen seq to avoid duplication.

3) Structured output framing and validation
   - Structured_chunk frames carry a schema_id and an optional checksum. SDK validates chunks incrementally and exposes typed objects to caller (TS types generated from schema_id).
   - Checkpoint frames signal a safe commit point for client-side local caching and resumption.

4) SDK ergonomics (JS/TS playbook)
   - Surface: Session.create(options) -> Session object with methods: on('frame', cb), await nextCheckpoint(), callTool(toolSpec), resumeFrom(seq)
   - High-level helper: Session.renderAs('document') returns an async iterator of high-level events: {type:'partial', text:'..'} | {type:'tool', id:'..', result:..} | {type:'structured', schema:'..', obj:..}
   - Backpressure: SDK exposes low-level pausing API (session.pauseStream()) and automatically sets a "client-window" header indicating how many frames/bytes it can accept.

5) Prefetch hints (server optimization knobs)
   - request metadata fields client_prefetch_budget (tokens), expected_response_shape (e.g., {type: 'list', avg_item_length: 120}), interactive_priority (low/med/high)
   - Server uses these hints to pick kernels, batch windows, and model variants (cheaper quantized variant vs low-latency full float).

Operational and observability notes
- Telemetry events to emit: frame_emit(latency_ms), tool_handshake_latency, tool_result_size, checkpoint_committed(seq), frame_parse_errors.
- Billing implications: partial frames count toward token-metering model; checkpointed commits can be used to reconcile billable segments vs preview segments (policy TBD).

Developer migration playbook (rough)
1) Opt-in: new session param streaming_mode: 'typed-v1' on existing generation endpoint.
2) Client: adopt Session SDK and wire simple on('partial') handler to avoid full patching.
3) After rollout: enable tool-handshake for safe tool migrations behind feature flag.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Checkpoint semantics: should a checkpoint imply waiving of retries older than seq N? (ops implication)
- Billing model for prefetch previews vs committed output — product to own decision.
- How much schema validation server-side vs SDK-side? (tradeoff: latency vs correctness)
- Should we support binary frames (protobuf) alongside JSON for ultra-low-latency paths?

Next steps / TODOs
- [ ] Engineering spike: implement minimal frame router + echo toy server (backend: serving-runtime) — owners: Marco + Riley (2w)
- [ ] SDK PoC (TS async iterator) — owner: Sana (1w)
- [ ] Confluence: canonical handshake doc and sequence diagrams (link above) — owner: Evelyn (this doc->canonical)
- [ ] Product decision: billing for previews (ask finance) — owner: product

Notes to self
- Keep the frame model intentionally small to ease cross-language SDKs. Avoid introducing too many frame types in v1.
- Examples above intentionally show JSON-inline payloads to keep debugging simple over SSE; we can revisit compact binary later.

Feedback requested
- Does the session-first API feel intuitive for embedding UX teams? Where will they struggle?
- Are the prefetch hints actionable enough for serving-runtime to change kernel selection?

References
- internal: RDW-2351 (prefetch telemetry), GH-412 (sdk-iterator-poc), Confluence spec link above.

-- end of sketch --
